questions.stem: Use a dot diagram argument to explain why the sum of the first \(n\) odd positive integers is \(n^2\).
questions.hint: Think about building a square grid of dots by adding successive L-shaped borders.
questions.solution:
To visualize the sum of odd numbers, we can arrange dots in concentric L-shaped borders (called gnomons) starting from a single dot in the corner.
- The 1st shell has \(1\) dot.
- The 2nd shell adds \(3\) dots to make a \(2 \times 2\) square.
- The 3rd shell adds \(5\) dots to make a \(3 \times 3\) square.
- In general, the \(n\)-th shell adds \(2n-1\) dots to a square of side \(n-1\) to form a square of side \(n\). Therefore, \(1 + 3 + 5 + \dots + (2n-1) = n^2\).

steps.explain: Consider arranging dots in a square grid of size \(n \times n\). The total number of dots is \(n^2\).
We can partition this square into L-shaped shells starting from the top-left corner.
Adding these shells consecutively builds the square, demonstrating the identity.
